title: Fuel Charging and Controls: Before Diagnosis
introduction:
I start here by checking the diagnostic groundwork. Ford's diagnostic practices are the map legend: understanding them makes the later instructions much easier to read without guessing what a test expects.

This page identifies that prerequisite and the reference to use when the engine controller reports a fault code. It is an entry point to diagnosis; equipment, test conditions, measurements and corrective branches belong to the referenced procedures.

edits.text: These diagnostics assume a certain level of diagnostic skill and familiarity with Ford-specific diagnostic practices. For the explanation of those practices, refer to Diagnostic Methods (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation).
edits.why: That assumed knowledge is a prerequisite, not a missing step you should have to improvise. Read the methods reference if those practices are unfamiliar before continuing into the diagnostics.

edits.text: If a PCM DTC—a diagnostic trouble code from the powertrain control module—is present, refer to Electronic Engine Controls (303-14D Electronic Engine Controls - 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: This referral identifies where code-based diagnosis continues for the specified engine. The code alone does not supply the test sequence or justify a component replacement.
